changes.summary: Added the 14-day extension maintaining the arch construction restraint through December 3 or an earlier injunction ruling.
Added the pending Supreme Court emergency stay application and preserved the government's asserted operational effects as party claims.
Added the announced $400 million Philippine FMF use and separately proposed loan package above $2 billion.
Added the secretary's testimony that incomplete ICE background checks or full training now trigger administrative leave.
Added the announced signed U.S.–Venezuela military-cooperation agreement while keeping terms and implementation unresolved.

evidence_extracts.arch_extension: AP and Reuters reported that the operative November 5 restraint was extended 14 days; AP gave December 3 or an earlier injunction ruling as the endpoint.
evidence_extracts.tps_application: Official application 26A714 seeks an administrative and pending-appeal stay and labels release, removal and work-authorization effects as government representations.
evidence_extracts.philippines_fmf: The White House announced intended use of $400 million in FMF and said a separate loan package above $2 billion will be pursued.
evidence_extracts.ice_safeguards: AP reported Mullin's current-service background-check and training testimony and separately corrected what he did not acknowledge about prior practice.
evidence_extracts.venezuela_military_agreement: AP and Reuters independently reported Hegseth's public announcement of a signed military-cooperation agreement covering training and intelligence sharing; neither published the agreement text.
